tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/show_notes_structure.py
  tests/test_show_notes_structure.py

WHY. Show notes are generated ad hoc with no defined structure. The owner wants every episode's notes to follow ONE shape that always includes: the guest's own words from the recording, the guest's contact details, the guest's headshot, a short bio, and the owner's booking link so a listener can book time with him. A 42-word run-on also shipped in the last approved notes, so the structure builder must be mechanically clean.

BUILD server/pipeline/show_notes_structure.py — pure stdlib, deterministic, NO model calls (a generator may fill prose fields; this module defines and assembles the STRUCTURE and validates it).

  SECTIONS: an ordered tuple of section ids defining the canonical shape:
      ("hook", "guest_intro", "in_this_episode", "quotes", "about_guest",
       "connect_with_guest", "resources", "about_show", "book_with_host", "listen")
  Document each in a module docstring: what it contains and whether it is REQUIRED.
  REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("hook", "in_this_episode", "quotes", "connect_with_guest", "book_with_host")

  build_show_notes(*, episode_number, title, hook, guest, highlights, quotes,
                   resources=None, show_url, booking_link, headshot=None) -> dict
    Returns a structured dict with one entry per section id plus a "meta" block.
    - guest: {"name","title","bio","links":{...},"email":...,"headshot_path"/"headshot_url"}
      In connect_with_guest, include only links the caller supplied; NEVER invent a
      handle or URL. Include the guest's email ONLY when guest.get("share_email") is
      truthy — a guest's address is not published by default.
    - quotes: list of {"text","timestamp_s","speaker"}. Each quote MUST carry a
      timestamp and speaker; a quote without them is a ValueError, because an
      unattributed quote is how invented content gets published.
    - highlights: list of {"timestamp_s","label"} rendered as timestamped bullets.
    - book_with_host: always renders the booking_link with a short human line.
      Missing/blank booking_link is a ValueError — the owner asked for it on every
      episode, so silently omitting it is a defect.
    - headshot: optional {"path" or "url", "credit"}; recorded in meta so the
      publisher can attach it.

  render_markdown(notes) -> str
    Deterministic markdown. Timestamps formatted H:MM:SS (or M:SS under an hour) from
    seconds. Quotes rendered as blockquotes with speaker and timestamp attribution.

  validate_show_notes(notes, *, max_sentence_words=38) -> list[str]
    Returns human-readable problems, empty when clean. Checks: every REQUIRED section
    present and non-empty; at least MIN_QUOTES (2) quotes each with speaker+timestamp;
    at least MIN_HIGHLIGHTS (4) highlights; booking link present and an http(s) URL;
    no sentence in any prose field longer than max_sentence_words (the 42-word run-on
    incident); no placeholder text left behind (case-insensitive TODO, TBD, XXX,
    "lorem", "{{" ).
    IMPORTANT: if server.pipeline.content_mechanics is importable, ALSO run its
    check_mechanics over the prose fields and merge its violations in; degrade
    gracefully (no crash) when it is absent.

TESTS (tests/test_show_notes_structure.py; at least 6): (1) a fully populated build passes validate with zero problems and render_markdown contains the booking link, both quotes with speaker and timestamp, and every required heading; (2) NEGATIVE: a quote missing its timestamp or speaker raises ValueError; (3) NEGATIVE: a blank/missing booking_link raises ValueError; (4) NEGATIVE: validate flags a 42-word run-on in the hook (use a real 42-word sentence) and flags leftover "TODO"; (5) the guest email is ABSENT from rendered output unless share_email is true, and present when it is; (6) timestamp formatting: 65 -> "1:05", 3725 -> "1:02:05"; (7) NEGATIVE: fewer than MIN_QUOTES or MIN_HIGHLIGHTS is reported by validate; (8) links the caller did not supply never appear in connect_with_guest.
tasks.verified: canonical show-notes structure with guest quotes, contact, headshot and the host booking link, validated against run-ons and placeholders

tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no live Gmail calls — the Gmail client is INJECTED and mocked in tests.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 5 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py
  tests/test_guest_email_context.py

WHY. Show notes need real context about the guest: how they describe themselves, the links they sent, and their headshot. That material usually already sits in the email thread with the guest. Today nothing reads it, so bios get scraped from the web and headshots go missing.

BUILD server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py — stdlib + the repo's existing email client passed IN (never constructed inside, so tests inject a fake):

  gather_guest_email_context(client, guest_email, *, max_messages=20) -> dict
    Search the guest's thread(s) by address and return:
      {"messages_scanned": int, "bio_candidates": [str], "links": {"linkedin": ..,
       "website": .., "instagram": .., "other": [..]}, "headshots": [{"filename",
       "mime_type", "size_bytes", "message_id", "attachment_id"}], "quotes": [str],
       "source_message_ids": [..]}
    - bio_candidates: paragraphs the GUEST wrote about themselves. Only consider
      messages FROM the guest address; never treat the host's own words as guest bio.
      Prefer paragraphs of 25-120 words that use first person.
    - links: extract http(s) URLs from guest messages and classify by host
      (linkedin.com, instagram.com, x.com/twitter.com, everything else -> other).
      De-duplicate. Never invent a link.
    - headshots: image attachments (mime image/*) from guest messages, or messages
      whose filename suggests a headshot. Return METADATA ONLY here.
    Strip quoted-reply blocks (lines starting with ">" and everything after a
    common "On <date> ... wrote:" separator) before extracting, so the host's
    quoted text is not mined as guest bio. That is the main correctness risk.

  download_headshot(client, headshot, dest_dir) -> str
    Fetch the attachment bytes via the injected client and write to dest_dir using a
    SAFE filename derived from the attachment (basename only, no directory traversal,
    extension restricted to a known image allowlist). Verify the payload actually
    begins with a known image magic number (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WEBP) and raise ValueError
    on mismatch — a mislabelled attachment must not be written as an image.
    Return the written path.

  SAFETY, enforce in code and assert in tests: never return or log the full body of
  any message; only the extracted fields. Never write outside dest_dir. Cap total
  downloaded bytes at MAX_HEADSHOT_BYTES (named constant, 10 MB) and raise past it.

TESTS (tests/test_guest_email_context.py, fake client object; at least 5): (1) a bio paragraph the guest wrote is returned while the host's quoted reply block in the SAME message is excluded — the key negative; (2) links are classified and de-duplicated, and a link only the host sent is not attributed to the guest; (3) an image/png attachment from the guest is listed as a headshot while a PDF is not; (4) NEGATIVE: download_headshot raises on a payload whose magic number is not an image, and on a filename attempting directory traversal (../../etc/passwd); (5) NEGATIVE: a payload over MAX_HEADSHOT_BYTES raises; (6) messages from addresses other than the guest are ignored entirely; (7) the returned dict never contains a raw message body (assert no full-body string is present).
tasks.verified: guest bio, links and headshot mined from the guest's own email messages, quoted-reply safe, with a magic-number-checked attachment download
